jobs.description:
The Exoplanet Group at DTU Space, Technical University of Denmark, invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship exoplanet science. Our group focuses on the discovery and characterization of small planets, from rocky worlds to super-Earths and sub-Neptunes. We combine observations, data analysis, modeling, and instrument development to understand the properties and diversity of these planets and the processes that shape their evolution.

Our research has two particularly active areas. In atmospheric characterization, we study the atmospheres of small exoplanets using observations from both space- and ground-based observatories, aiming to understand their composition, evolution, and retention. Much of our current research draws on the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), for which our group has led several successful observing programs (GO 2420, GO 3730, and GO 7675), alongside our involvement in numerous international collaborations, including involvement in ESA's Ariel Mission (Buchhave co-PI).

In extreme-precision radial velocity (EPRV) research, we work toward detecting and measuring low-mass planets, including through the Second Earth Spectrograph (2ES; PI: Buchhave; www.2es.dk). 2ES is a next-generation spectrograph under development for the MPG/ESO 2.2-m Telescope at La Silla, Chile, designed to search for temperate Earth-mass planets around bright southern solar-type stars. The project spans instrumentation, data analysis, stellar activity, and the preparation for commissioning and early science.

Our aim is to recruit a researcher whose scientific interests and expertise complement the group's work. The successful candidate will be free to pursue the questions in exoplanet science that they find most compelling, whether these connect directly to our current projects or bring related perspectives and methods to the group.

We consider an open and cooperative research atmosphere to be extremely important. Group members take an interest in one another's science, exchange ideas, and explore opportunities to work together. We hope to welcome a colleague who enjoys participating in such an environment while developing their own independent research.

You will join Prof. Lars A. Buchhave and Assistant Prof. Alexander Rathcke, and the growing Exoplanet Group at DTU Space (www.exoplanets.dk), located in the greater Copenhagen area. The group has access to data from world-class observatories, including JWST, precision RV spectrographs, and ESO facilities, and collaborates widely with researchers abroad.

Responsibilities and qualifications
We expect the successful candidate to develop and carry out original, independent research that complements the group's scientific interests. The specific direction will be shaped by the candidate's own interests and expertise. Possible research topics include:

 * Characterizing exoplanet atmospheres through transmission or emission spectroscopy, atmospheric retrievals and modeling, JWST data analysis, or studies of stellar contamination.

 * Detecting and characterizing low-mass planets through precision radial velocities, including RV data analysis, stellar activity mitigation, spectroscopic pipeline development, or 2ES instrumentation.

 * Pursuing other closely related observational, theoretical, or computational questions that complement the group's research on exoplanets.

We are seeking a talented and highly motivated student to work at the cutting edge of the rapidly moving research field of exoplanets. Applicants with previous experience in the mentioned areas of research are especially encouraged to apply, and we particularly value scientific initiative and strong analytical skills. Flexibility and self-motivation are desired skills, and the Exoplanet Group encourages a vibrant collaborative work environment, where collaboration with other group members is highly encouraged. In your application, we encourage you to describe how you can complement the group's scientific activities.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is flexible but would ideally commence in Q3-Q4 of 2027.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information and inquiries about the position can be made to Prof. Lars A. Buchhave (buchhave@space.dtu.dk) or Dr. Alexander Rathcke (rathcke@space.dtu.dk).

You can read more about the Exoplanet Group at www.exoplanets.dk and the DTU Space institute at www.space.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 22 January 2027 (23:59 Danish time).

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• Research statement describing your previous work and thoughts and ideas for future research (max 3 pages)
Shortlisted candidates will be asked to provide 2-3 reference letters to be emailed at a later date.

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

About DTU Space
The DTU Space Institute has about 250 employees and is located in the greater Copenhagen area at the Lyngby Campus of the Technical University of Denmark. We link natural science closely with the development of new technology. DTU Space is involved in the full life cycle of space activities, including concept and design, construction and prototyping, calibration and validation, implementation and operations, data analysis, processing, dissemination, and applications, leading to new instruments and applications. With the specialised and refined technology available, we are getting more and more answers and further insight about the Earth and the universe surrounding us. We contribute to about 200 scientific publications a year.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Do you love turning menus and interfaces into something players actually enjoy clicking through, and want to own that from first sketch to final implementation? We’d love to talk to you.

Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by a simple mission: to make everyone laugh.

We're working on our most ambitious project to date: a new systemic open-world game built around a beloved IP, with our own spin on it. A bold new direction for us! And we're just getting started.

Now, we’re looking for a UI/UX Designer to join a team of around 15-20 people and own the UI/UX for the entire game. You’ll be the first dedicated UI/UX designer on the team (and at Triband generally!), so you’ll shape the game’s interface aesthetic and logic as well as player experience from the ground up.

**Here’s What You’ll Do Day To Day

**

• Own the full UI/UX pipeline for the game: from flow, wireframes, and mockups through to final in-engine implementation (we use Unity)

• Design and build UI elements like menus, icons, HUDs, and input controls that are clear, playful, and true to the game’s tone

• Bake in accessibility design and settings from the start, not as an afterthought

• Create dynamic transitions and animations that make the UI feel alive

• Implement your own designs solidly in Unity (you won’t be just handing off mockups!)

• Collaborate closely with game designers and programmers to keep the UI consistent, technically sound, and fun to use

• Maintain a consistent visual language and set of UI standards as the game grows

**You’re probably a good match if

**

• You have solid experience owning UI/UX work end to end, from flow through to final implementation

• You have strong Unity implementation skills and are comfortable taking your own UI work all the way into engine

• You’re skilled in Illustrator

• You have experience mocking up interactive flows in a tool like Figma, Miro, or similar (any tool is fine)

• You genuinely enjoy working within an existing visual style rather than starting from a blank page every time

• You’ve shipped a mobile game before, including responsive/adaptive interfaces

**Nice to have

• A passion for accessibility and usability, especially for family-friendly/casual audiences

• You see real value in user testing and what it can teach you

• You’re motivated by collaboration, mutual respect, inclusiveness, and creativity, and you actively contribute to sustaining that culture.

• You bring curiosity, generosity, and flexibility, along with strong opinions, especially when they come with reasoning, openness, and a willingness to actually test them.

• You’re up for experimentation, and at the same time you don’t get too precious when the experience tells you you’re wrong.

• You value a positive work environment and contribute to keeping the studio a fun and supportive place.

**

• We work on-site at our cozy office in central Copenhagen.

• This role is based in the Greater Copenhagen area, and we’re not considering people located outside of commuting distance for this one.

• We work a 37-hour work week, with core hours 10–15, and the freedom to start and finish anywhere between 7 and 18.

• Our working language is English.

**We offer

**

• A shot at shaping the interface of a live game played by millions

• A tight, collaborative team where your ideas actually make it into the game

• A playful work environment where trying the silly idea is encouraged

• Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games

**Data Science Student in Strategy & Transformation

Who We Are

**NNIT is a niche specialist in IT for life sciences and highly regulated industries. We help pharma, biotech and medtech companies across Europe, the US and Asia, as well as public sector and regulated customers in Denmark, solve their most complex challenges where technology, regulation and business critical processes meet.

We are in the middle of a fundamental transformation. Our strategy, OneNNIT 2030, sets out how we will sharpen our position as a niche specialist, reshape our portfolio into a focused set of value pathways that take customers from advisory through implementation to managed services, bring our US and European organisations together as one, and become a genuinely AI-driven company.

The Strategy & Transformation Office leads that journey. It reports directly to our CEO, owns NNIT's strategy cycle, runs the transformation programme and builds the capabilities that will carry the momentum through to 2030. We are now building the team, and we are looking for a Data Science Student who wants to work at the heart of it.

**What You Will Do

**You will be part of the analytical engine in the Strategy & Transformation Office. Every major decision in our transformation needs a solid fact base, and every initiative needs to show that it delivers. You will help build both, and your work will land directly with our CEO and Executive Management.

You are comfortable with code and data, and just as interested in what the numbers mean for the business. You are AI savvy, and you are curious about the bigger picture of how AI transforms organisations, ways of working and business models.

**Typical tasks include

**▪ Building the fact base behind OneNNIT 2030, from portfolio and revenue analysis to customer, market and capability data

▪ Designing and maintaining the KPIs, dashboards and benefit tracking that show Executive Management and the Board how the transformation is progressing

▪ Modelling revenue, margin and demand across offerings and geographies as we consolidate our portfolio into value pathways

▪ Combining data from finance, sales, delivery and HR systems into analyses that inform strategic decisions

▪ Identifying, sizing and prioritising AI use cases across our offerings, delivery model and internal processes, and tracking AI adoption across NNIT

▪ Building prototypes and analytical tools in Python, SQL or Power BI, and using generative AI to work faster and smarter

▪ Turning analysis into clear insights and material for workshops, leadership meetings and strategy sessions

**What You Will Bring

****We imagine that you

**▪ Are preferably in the third year of your Bachelor's degree, or in the first year of your Master’s degree, for example in Business ▪ Administration and Data Science or Digital Management at Copenhagen Business School

▪ Have a strong interest in data science, AI, strategy and business transformation

▪ Are curious about how data and AI change decisions, organisations and value creation

▪ Are analytical and structured, and able to turn complex data into clear insights that non-specialists can act on

▪ Have hands-on experience with Python and SQL, and with Power BI or a similar tool, alongside strong Excel and PowerPoint skills

▪ Communicate clearly and professionally in Danish and English, both written and spoken

▪ Take initiative, have a strong eye for quality, handle confidential information with discretion and enjoy working with senior stakeholders

**What We Offer

**You will join the Strategy & Transformation Office, which reports directly to the CEO, and work closely with the Head of Strategy & Transformation. You will have a front-row seat as NNIT redefines its strategy, organisation and portfolio, and you will work alongside Executive Management, senior leaders across Europe, the US and Asia, and our external advisors.

You will get real responsibility from day one, high exposure to senior leadership and the flexibility to balance work with your studies. Few student jobs offer a closer view of how strategy and transformation are done in practice.

**Practical Information

**The role is 15 to 20 hours per week, with flexibility around exams.

Please upload your CV and cover letter in English. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply soon.

**About NNIT

**NNIT is a publicly listed company that specializes in IT solutions to life sciences internationally, and to the public and enterprise sectors in Denmark. We focus on high complexity industries and thrive in environments where regulatory demands and complexity are high. We advise on and build sustainable digital solutions that work for the patients, citizens, employees, end users or customers.

NNIT consists of group company NNIT A/S and subsidiaries SCALES, Excellis Health Solutions and SL Controls. Together, these companies employ more than 1,600 people in Europe, Asia, and USA.

We celebrate diversity and are dedicated to fostering an inclusive environment for all employees. We actively work to eliminate bias and ensure an inclusive workplace where everyone has the right to be seen and heard as they are. We invite interested candidates to apply, no matter their background.

In the interest of fostering a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly request candidates to refrain from including their pictures in their applications.
